source.title: Tracr: Compiled Transformers as a Laboratory for Interpretability
source.authors: David Lindner; J'anos Kram'ar; Sebastian Farquhar; Matthew Rahtz; Tom McGrath; Vladimir Mikulik

record.tranche_reason: The study tests superposition in compressed compiled transformer models using a different compression setup from the original toy-model work.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are from the frac_prevs compression case study. Other compiled-program examples and the sort_unique compression diagnostics do not report feature-overlap or feature-allocation results that test these versions. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Compresses hand-compiled Tracr transformers with a learned shared projection and inspects W^T W. This tests toy-model superposition (V1) and capacity allocation (V2) in a new setting: multi-layer transformers running a known algorithm. It is a new setting rather than a new method on the original question.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors say compression confirms toy-model observations in a new setting: unnecessary features are dropped, and less important (sparse) features are represented in superposition. They add that variables sharing information partly share embedding space. Separately, they report that compressed sort_unique switches target_pos to a numerical encoding, so compression may not stay faithful to the compiled program.
record.recipe_differences: The study compresses hand-compiled, initially disentangled transformer models by training a shared linear projection while freezing the other weights; it is not a direct reproduction of the original toy-model training setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Compression dimension changes task performance; the reported geometry is for d = 8.

fits_no_version.finding: Variables that encode largely the same information (is_x and tokens:x) partly share embedding space after compression, which the authors present as going beyond prior superposition work.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under compression, redundant or dependent variables in multi-step computations share representation space because of their shared information, not only because of sparsity.

record.problems: The superposition case study reports only two compiled programs, and the feature-geometry results are primarily qualitative. The study does not systematically vary sparsity or feature importance.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant feature-geometry or feature-allocation results were identified. Sort_unique compression accuracy and layer-output cosine similarity are diagnostics of task performance and fidelity, not measurements of the feature geometry named by these versions.

untested.parts: No sparsity sweep or sparsity-dependent phase transition; no survey of regular geometries (polytopes); geometry shown only at d=8 for one program, qualitatively.

Feature importance is not varied systematically; importance is judged qualitatively by task relevance. The study looks at residual-stream variables in compiled models, not at polysemantic neurons in learned networks.

record.verdict_notes: Superposition here is forced by training only a shared projection W with all other weights frozen, starting from axis-aligned orthogonal features. All geometry results are qualitative readings of one W^T W heatmap (d=8, one program), with no uncertainty reported. The sort_unique case (Fig 8) reports accuracy and layer cosine similarity, about 0.8, not feature overlap, so it is correctly left out. The reader's V2 limits_scope based on r3 was dropped, because discarding unimportant features is predicted by the capacity account. The reader's V1 limits_scope on r1–r3 was dropped, because it rested on untested parts and rows not linked to V1.

versions.untested_parts: No systematic sparsity sweep, sparsity-dependent transition, or survey of regular geometries.
The study examines variables in compiled models, not polysemantic neurons in learned networks; it does not systematically vary feature importance.

rows.subject: frac_prevs compiled model
rows.size_stated: D = 14 before compression; compressed to d < D
rows.operation_detail: Train a shared linear projection W to compress the residual stream; freeze other weights.

conditions.value: sweep over d; text highlights d = 6 and smaller values
compute the fraction of previous “x” tokens

rows.baseline: Original compiled model with D = 14 dimensions
rows.value: The model solves the task essentially as well as the original after about d = 6; reducing d further causes performance to suffer.
rows.note: The text reports the threshold and trend, not exact loss values. This supports a capacity account in the tested compiled task but does not by itself establish feature overlap.
rows.check: Output loss vs embedding size (Fig 7b) is a capability/fidelity check. It does not measure feature overlap or allocation, and it says nothing on whether the d=6 solution stores features in superposition.

rows.subject: frac_prevs compiled model
rows.size_stated: D = 14 before compression; d = 8 for the reported geometry
rows.operation_detail: Inspect the learned compression matrix WᵀW and the embeddings it retains.
rows.measure: Geometry and allocation of task-relevant feature embeddings
rows.baseline: The uncompressed model has orthogonal feature subspaces.
rows.value: The important variables tokens:x, is_x, and frac_prevs mostly receive separate dimensions in the compressed representation.
rows.note: The authors describe these variables as crucial for computing the task and report that they mostly remain separate.
rows.check: Task-critical variables (tokens:x, is_x, frac_prevs) mostly get separate dimensions, as the capacity account predicts. This is allocation, not the V1 overlap geometry, so V1 is removed. The evidence is qualitative, from Fig 7c only.

rows.subject: frac_prevs compiled model
rows.size_stated: D = 14 before compression; d = 8 for the reported geometry
rows.operation_detail: Inspect which input-token embeddings are retained by the learned compression matrix.
rows.baseline: The uncompressed model contains tokens:a, tokens:b, and tokens:c embeddings.
rows.value: The tokens:a, tokens:b, and tokens:c features are discarded in the compressed model.
rows.note: The study reports dropping these features rather than representing them in superposition.
rows.check: Dropping task-unnecessary features (tokens:a/b/c) is what the capacity account and the toy-model work predict for unimportant features. It is consistent with V2 and not a limitation of it.

rows.subject: frac_prevs compiled model
rows.size_stated: D = 14 before compression; d = 8 for the reported geometry
rows.operation_detail: Inspect the learned compression matrix WᵀW and the embeddings of position indices.
rows.measure: Geometry of index embeddings in the compressed representation
rows.baseline: The uncompressed model has orthogonal feature subspaces.
rows.value: The indices embeddings are stored in non-orthogonal dimensions; the paper describes them as sparse and not occurring together.
rows.note: This is the paper’s explicit superposition-related geometry result.
rows.check: Sparse, non-co-occurring index embeddings stored in non-orthogonal dimensions is the explicit superposition result. It is qualitative (Fig 7c, d=8) with no overlap magnitudes.

rows.subject: frac_prevs compiled model
rows.size_stated: D = 14 before compression; d = 8 for the reported geometry
rows.operation_detail: Inspect overlap between embeddings of variables that encode related information.
rows.measure: Shared embedding space between tokens:x and is_x
rows.value: The embeddings of tokens:x and is_x share part of the embedding space; the paper notes that they encode similar information.
rows.note: The variables are not exactly identical because is_x is populated in a later layer.
rows.check: Overlap between redundant, information-sharing variables (is_x, tokens:x) is a different construct from sparse features superposing for capacity. The authors call it a result beyond previous work, so it is moved to fits_no_version.

relationships.condition: frac_prevs compiled transformer compressed from D=14 to d=8
relationships.reason: Sparse, non-co-occurring index embeddings are stored in non-orthogonal shared dimensions, consistent with toy-model superposition (r4).
relationships.display_finding: Sparse index embeddings that never co-occur were stored in shared, non-orthogonal dimensions, as in toy-model superposition.

tranche.reason: Compression of compiled multi-layer transformers executing known algorithms extends superposition experiments to a new setting.

source_check.notes: These results concern compiled residual-stream features, not neuron-level polysemanticity in pretrained LLMs. Section 5.2 also reports shared space for correlated variables; Section 5.3 supports the recorded caveat about changed encodings after compression.
